rv.q: Nicholas Hytner’s perfectly pitched production of Richard Bean’s delirious comedy is sharp, silly and trimmer than at the outset: gloriously funny and a plum piece of seasonal entertainment.
The show, in short, is a tonic which confirms Eric Bentley's point that farce is the quintessence of theatre and which combines a tightly-written text with the gaiety of popular entertainment.
A hit or my name’s Francis Henshall.

cn.t: Critics hail this raucous Goldoni adaptation as a smash hit that transfers brilliantly to the West End, maintaining its freshness and generating uproarious laughter with pumped-up comic energy.
